articleTitle: The development and use of heat-shrinkable materials as high voltage power cable terminations
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The method of terminating high — voltage paper — insulated power cables has remained virtually unchanged in the last 50 years. Traditionally these involve cast or fabricated metal cable boxes filled with bitumen compound and sealed with lead wipe to the sheath of the cable. Heat-shrinkable materials have made possible an entirely new approach to the termination of these types of cable which is quickly replacing the older techniques for both indoor and outdoor use, to the extent that during the past three years over 3000 of such terminations have been installed throughout Europe. The purpose of this paper is to outline the differences between these materials and conventional thermoplastics and describe their evaluation and use as terminations for high-voltage power cables.

articleTitle: An incremental model for educational planning
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: A model has been formulated and discussed for use in the future planning of higher education. The model incorporates econometric constraints and the goals of education. Unlike other models the model developed in this paper is incremental in nature and contains an updating factor which is analogous to inserting a feedback loop. The model is intended for realistic short term forecasting which is in line with present day needs of accelerated change.

abstract: A digital position servo was constructed in which a stepper motor is used as the prime mover and pulses provide the source of drive, feedback information and computation. articleTitle: Load flow data base and solution, using a digital computer
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The first part of the paper describes the power system Data Base used by ESCOM to store and maintain its data for power system analysis, and in particular for load flow calculations. A simple command language enables the data to be manipulated directly from a computer terminal. The second part of the paper deals with the load flow calculation. A matrix inversion technique Is described. This is followed by a triangular matrix technique which uses the same basic equations as the matrix inversion method, but which takes advantage of the sparsity of the admittance matrix of the power system network to reduce the memory requirements as well as the computation time. All the necessary equations required for the load flow calculation are given in the appendices.

publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Thin film microcircuits containing selfhealing thin film capacitors have been manufactured in a small scale in-house production unit. The capacitors made had values ranging between 100 pF and 10 000 pF, The capacitance per unit area was 89 pF/mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The quality factor, Q. was greater than 1 000 for frequencies up to 1 MH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> and about 50 at a frequency of 20 MHz for capacitors having a value of about 300 pF. The method of production is described, in particular its incorporation into the existing manufacturing process for conductors and resistors, and measurement data presented.

articleTitle: Technology, design and automatic testing of a microcircuit thin film read-only memory
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: A read-only memory using resistors as coupling elements has been developed in thin film technology. The resistors are arranged in a 33 by 12 matrix on a 25 mm by 12.5 mm glass substrate. A dielectric layer insulates orthogonal drive and sense lines. Altogether the substrate contains 429 resistors and 384 insulated crossovers. A computer-controlled tester has also been developed to test these resistor matrices for faults and to verify the stored code.
